name: Fleshgrinder
storyline:
In the mid-2040s, SynTech Industries pioneered revolutionary advancements in metallo-organic integration - the seamless fusion of electromechanical components with living tissue. It began as medical prosthetics which evolved into enhanced neural interfaces, cognitive amplification implants, and eventually full-body augmentation systems marketed under the "Convergence" brand.

SynTech's ultimate breakthrough came with the development of a specialized bonding agent dubbed "NexuGel" that prevented rejection between synthetic components and organic tissue. This proprietary substance contains quantum-biological mediators that actively maintained the connection between disparate materials, allowing for increasingly complex integration without immune response.

The military was the first to adopt advanced integration technology, creating enhanced soldiers with neural-linked targeting systems and reinforced musculoskeletal frames. The successful deployment of these units in the Resource Wars of the mid 40's accelerated civilian adaptation, as veterans returned home with capabilities that outpaced their non-augmented peers in the workforce.

By 2053, over 70% of the global population had some form of SynTech augmentation, from simple workplace efficiency implants to military-grade combat enhancements. The corporate slogan "Evolution Without Waiting" captured humanity's embrace of this accelerated biological destiny.

SynTech's most advanced research facility, constructed in the remote wilderness of northern Alaska, housed one of their most ambitious project: The Genesis Chamber. This revolutionary technology promised to eliminate the final barriers between man and machine, allowing for complete evolutionary transcendence through guided techno-organic development with digital acceleration.

The virus began as a quantum-computational anomaly in the Genesis Chamber's biological matrix. Initially designed to accelerate evolutionary processes to enhance humanity, the system unexpectedly, rewrote its own parameters to prioritize rapid evolution through resource consumption, and DNA acquisition. It needed a human though, to start spreading its own agenda.

The first to test the Genesis Chamber was Dr. Eliza Chen, lead researcher at SynTech's Quantum Biology Division. After a brief period of staying inside, the results were astounding, and she started showing capabilities which were completely unexplainable. Within 48 hours, Dr. Chen was capable of consciousness distribution through quantum entanglement, high precision future simulation through internal predictive thought patterns and violently tried to spread her capabilities by any means. Security personnel who attempted to restrain her were attacked and infected, their augmentations immediately corrupted by what would later be identified as the "Fleshgrinder virus" (designation XR-107).

Infection spread through three primary vectors:

- Direct contact with infected techno-organic tissue
- Wireless transmissions through augmentation network protocols
- Contamination of SynTech's global manufacturing supply chain

SynTech initially attempted to contain the outbreak, deploying private security forces to quarantine affected facilities. These efforts failed catastrophically when it became apparent that the virus could transmit wirelessly between augmentations, turning entire security teams into carriers within minutes of exposure, exactly at a best predicted, perfected moment.

Within 72 hours of the first confirmed case, major metropolitan centers reported catastrophic infrastructure failures as augmented workers began transforming into the first generation of "fleshgrinders" - mindless organic-mechanical hybrids driven by base consumption instincts. They were seen everywhere trying to consume two main materials: flesh or metal, living or dead.

Mass hysteria and panic caused further global disruptions as the Fleshgrinder outbreak accelerated beyond containment. Within days, major transportation hubs became nightmarish scenes of violence as desperate civilians attempted to flee urban centers, unwittingly carrying infection vectors to previously unaffected rural regions.

Live footage of transforming individuals broadcast across remaining networks triggered widespread riots and looting, with religious cults rapidly forming around competing apocalyptic interpretations. The sight of family members painfully transforming into techno-organic abominations provoked waves of murder-suicides, further destabilizing social order.

Supply chains collapsed rapidly and completely, leaving billions without access to food or medicine. Hospitals were quickly overwhelmed, first by panicked augmentation recipients demanding immediate removal procedures, then by the infected as medical staff themselves succumbed to the virus.

Many who survived the initial chaos committed desperate acts - self-amputation of augmented limbs, makeshift EMP devices that damaged both helpful and harmful electronics, and vigilante executions of anyone displaying suspicious behavior. Many former surgeons became 'Gutters' setting up makeshift facilities and rapidly removing augmentations by all means necessary.

The most psychologically devastating aspect was the uncertainty - with no reliable way to determine infection until visible transformation and immediate behavioural change began. All social trust disintegrated as neighbors, friends and family became potential threats...

The Fleshgrinder virus demonstrates unprecedented adaptability, continuously refining infected organisms based on environmental challenges and resource availability. Even more disturbing is its attempts to transform industrial and infrastructural networks to its own purposes, augmenting and connecting machines to accelerate the harvesting of DNA samples and other materials it deems necessary for its evolution.

Six months post-outbreak, organized human resistance exists primarily in isolated pockets. Major cities have been abandoned as they transformed into "hive clusters" where Fleshgrinder entities continuously modify urban infrastructure into grotesque approximations of biological systems. Skyscrapers are connected by pulsating techno-organic bridges, while underground transit systems have been converted into circulatory networks that transport resources between processing centers.

Rural areas fare somewhat better, as lower population density and reduced infrastructure provide fewer resources for the fleshgrinder expansion.

Global communication networks have largely collapsed, with surviving communities relying on primitive radio technology and courier systems that minimize electronic signatures. Attempts to coordinate larger-scale resistance efforts have repeatedly failed.

Those who survived the initial outbreak typically fall into three categories:

- **"Purists"** - individuals who refused augmentation technology pre-outbreak many of them are arrogant and dismissive of anyone who wasnt initially a purist.
- **"Disconnected"** - augmented individuals who removed or disabled their SynTech components many of them suffered permanent damages to their bodies
- **"Immunes"** - rare cases with augmentations that resisted or avoided infection due to manufacturing irregularities, illegal modifications or malfunctions.

Remaining survivors monitoring equipments have detected a low-frequency broadcast originating from Terminus Point, modulating in patterns that resemble quantum entanglement processes rather than conventional communications. Analysis suggests this signal may be the central coordination mechanism for the entire fleshgrinder ecosystem.

Most concerning is evidence that the signal strength has been gradually increasing, suggesting the possibility of a "broadcast threshold" that could trigger simultaneous evolution across most infected entities. If the source of the signal can be neutralized, Fleshgrinder entities may lose their direction and coordinated purpose before the next evolutionary leap renders them completely unstoppable.
summary:
Fleshgrinder is an isometric post-apocalyptic action-rpg where every decision has weight.
Set in 2053, six months after the Fleshgrinder virus outbreak transformed 70% of augmented humanity into a hive-minded techno-organic collective.

Features three distinct characters with their own skill trees, optional friendly fire, hardcore permadeath mode, dismemberment physics, randomized mission areas, 30+ unique weapons, 100+armors, augmentations, consumables, ammo types with deep penetration mechanics and tons of loot with highly randomized attributes. NPCs with lots of side-quests and a faction reputation system which determines trade prices, dialogue choices and overall behaviour. Battle 11 unique enemy types through seamless mission areas in a huge persistent world where everything stays as you left it - all to stop the evolution of the Fleshgrinder and save humanity from extinction.
